subject.title: [Feature]: Add bounded/validated append semantics for pre-compaction memory flush

question: Should OpenClaw accept a strict built-in daily-memory append policy for memory-flush writes as the default behavior, as proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96291?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but changing memory-flush writes from always-append to reject/skip/sanitize by default is a session-state compatibility and security-boundary product decision.

options.title: Accept strict built-in guard
options.body: Land a wrapper-level daily-memory policy with conservative size limits, scaffold rejection, duplicate skipping, and structured telemetry as the default.

options.title: Request compatible rollout
options.body: Keep existing appends as the default and introduce bounded validation through an explicit maintainer-approved compatibility or opt-in path.

options.title: Redesign as plugin/runtime hook
options.body: Pause the current PR and define a typed validation extension point before implementing daily-memory policy in core.

recommendation.title: Accept strict built-in guard
recommendation.body: Land a wrapper-level daily-memory policy with conservative size limits, scaffold rejection, duplicate skipping, and structured telemetry as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the original memory-flush feature, memory plugin ownership, security defaults, and compatibility policy.
